events.subtitle: Seeing in the Dark — two world premieres
events.category: New music / world premieres / large ensemble
events.factual_description: Roulette presents Contemporaneous, Mantra Percussion, and Recap Percussion in Seeing in the Dark on Tuesday, October 20, 2026 at 8:00 PM, with doors at 7:00 PM and free admission with RSVP. Contemporaneous identifies the event as its 2026-27 season opener. The program includes Lila Meretzky's to crave and to have; the world premiere of a chamber-orchestral arrangement of Brendon Randall-Myers and Annie Blythe's cello concerto Only in the Dark, with Blythe as soloist; and the world premiere of Paul Pinto's America: Book Two, performed with Mantra Percussion and Recap Percussion. Roulette describes Pinto's work as the next book in his years-in-the-making meta-opera Estabanico. The primary event pages announce the ensembles, composers, and Blythe but do not publish complete individual personnel rosters for Contemporaneous, Mantra Percussion, or Recap Percussion, so no additional musicians are inferred.

en.why_it_matters: This is not simply another new-music bill at Roulette. Contemporaneous opens its season by putting chamber-orchestral color and two percussion ensembles around two premieres: Annie Blythe's cello voice pushed into the larger architecture of Only in the Dark, and the next stage of Paul Pinto's long-form historical meta-opera. The scale and contrast make the program feel like a composed argument about how contemporary music can carry private sensory experience and contested history in the same room.
en.trip_verdict: If New York is already workable on October 20, actively make room for this Roulette night and let it anchor the evening. From the DMV, I would pair the Brooklyn trip with another strong New York reason rather than make the round trip solely for this program.

es.why_it_matters: No es simplemente otra noche de música nueva en Roulette. Contemporaneous abre su temporada poniendo color orquestal de cámara y dos ensambles de percusión alrededor de dos estrenos: la voz del cello de Annie Blythe expandida en la arquitectura de Only in the Dark y el siguiente tramo de la meta-ópera histórica de largo aliento de Paul Pinto. La escala y el contraste hacen que el programa funcione como un argumento compuesto sobre cómo la música contemporánea puede cargar experiencia sensorial íntima e historia disputada dentro del mismo espacio.
es.trip_verdict: Si Nueva York ya es viable el 20 de octubre, le abriría espacio activamente a esta noche en Roulette y dejaría que ancle la salida. Desde el DMV, juntaría el viaje a Brooklyn con otra razón fuerte en Nueva York en vez de hacer toda la ida y vuelta únicamente por este programa.
